\nКак и в настоящем времени, в имперфект: As in the present, the middle and passive voices have the same form in the imperfect. It is formed like the active one: the augment, the connecting vowel and the secondary middle-passive personal endings are attached to the stem.
\nВ пассивном значении те же формы перев: In the passive sense the same forms are translated differently: {{1}} — “I was being untied”, {{2}} — “you were being untied”, and so on. Deponent verbs also have a middle-passive form in the imperfect: {{3}} (I come) — {{4}} (I was coming).
\nПри подлежащем среднего рода во множес: With a neuter plural subject the predicate usually stands in the singular:
\nРеже сказуемое стоит и во множественно: Less often the predicate stands in the plural too: {{1}} — the children are saved.
— «и», а также «также, даже»; в значени: — “and”, also “also, even”; in the sense “even” it stands before the word it refers to: {{1}} — even the children know the law.
— «и не, даже не, ни»: {{1}} — даже уче: — “and not, not even, nor”: {{1}} — not even the disciples see the glory of God.
\nВ греческом предложении может быть тол: A Greek sentence can contain only one negation — a single negative particle or conjunction for the whole clause, unlike Russian.
